Christian Kontz

Working Papers


Do financial markets price carbon emissions? Evidence from auto ABS

Abstract:

Securitized auto loans contain substantial amounts of non-taxed externalities in the form of CO2 emissions. The emissions content of auto ABS varies substantially across and within issuer. I provide evidence that primary and secondary security markets do not price these differences despite the massive rise in ESG investing over the past decade. If markets were to fully internalize the emissions embedded in auto ABS, average issuance spreads would need to increase seven fold if the true current social cost of carbon is $51 per tonne of CO2. This additional spread is heterogeneous across issuers and consumer groups with sub-prime issues seeing the largest increases. Lastly, I find no evidence that commitments to reduce emissions by banks that serve as active book runners have an effect on issuance spreads or security design.
